issues.description: Duplicate literal "transcriber_error" in the error-type tuple — evidence of unreasoned enumeration
issues.detail: The tuple of message_type values contains "transcriber_error" twice. A reader who had stated the postcondition ("every documented error type produces exactly one push_error") and constructed the set by reasoning rather than by copy-paste would not have written the same identifier twice. The duplication is harmless to runtime (tuple membership is idempotent), but it is a direct symptom of the author building the set by enumeration without checking it against a specification. The set should be derived from, and named after, the documented list — ideally a module-level constant ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES — and the duplicate removed.

issues.description: No stated specification for the new _receive_messages: precondition, postcondition, and termination are left implicit
issues.detail: The PR description correctly identifies that the prior try/except around _process_messages turned a websocket disconnect into a silently-swallowed exception, which the outer reconnect loop then converted into an infinite loop. The fix removes the try/except, which is correct. But the new method ships with a one-line docstring and no statement of: (a) precondition — _get_websocket() yields an open async iterator; (b) postcondition — on normal close, return; on error, raise so the outer loop in websocket_service.py can decide to reconnect or back off; (c) termination — the async-for terminates when the iterator is exhausted or raises. Without these stated, the next maintainer who sees an unhandled exception will reintroduce the same try/except and the bug will return. Add the contract to the docstring.

issues.description: Inner try/except Exception inside the async-for is a defensive-programming substitute for reasoning about message shape
issues.detail: The remaining try/except inside _receive_messages catches json.JSONDecodeError (reasonable) and then catches bare Exception and logs it. That bare except is precisely the construct that produced the infinite-loop bug being fixed: it converts arbitrary failures inside _process_response into a log line and continues the loop. If _process_response raises because the websocket connection is half-broken, or because of a programming error in a handler, this except will swallow it forever. The author should state which exception classes _process_response is permitted to raise under a well-formed message and let everything else propagate. "Catch Exception and log" is DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE for knowing the message contract.

issues.description: Outer reconnect loop in websocket_service.py is the actual locus of the bug and is not audited in this PR
issues.detail: The PR description correctly diagnoses that _receive_messages is run inside an outer loop in websocket_service.py (lines 133-154) that retries on exception. The fix is applied at the wrong altitude: it removes the inner try/except so that exceptions propagate to the outer loop, on the assumption that the outer loop will then reconnect-or-exit correctly. But the outer loop's invariant — "on transient failure, reconnect with backoff; on permanent failure, exit" — is not stated or verified in this diff. If the outer loop also catches Exception and retries without backoff, the "infinite loop" merely moves up one frame. The reviewer should confirm that the outer loop has bounded retry, exponential backoff, or a termination condition, and cite the line. Otherwise this is TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: Error message types should be a named module-level constant, not an inline tuple literal
issues.detail: The list of error message types is documentation-derived data, not control flow. It belongs in a named constant — ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES = frozenset({...}) — at module scope, with a comment linking to the ElevenLabs docs URL the PR description references. This makes the precondition ("these are the documented error types as of <date>") explicit, makes drift from the upstream docs auditable, and prevents the duplicate-key class of bug from recurring. The elif then reads `elif message_type in ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES:` which is what the program is actually saying.

issues.description: Loss of per-error-type log context: all error types now emit the same generic push_error string
issues.detail: The prior code distinguished error / auth_error / quota_exceeded with distinct logger.error messages and distinct push_error prefixes. The new code collapses all fourteen error types into one branch and emits `Error: {error_msg}` with no logger.error call at all. The operator who sees "Error: Unknown error - rate_limited" in production has lost the explicit severity signal in the logs and lost the typed prefix in the pushed frame. At minimum, restore a logger.error(f"ElevenLabs {message_type}: {error_msg}") and include message_type in the push_error string. Consolidation is fine; loss of diagnostic information is not.

changelog/3233.fixed.md ends without a final newline (the diff shows "\ No newline at end of file"). This is a small discipline failure of the same kind as the duplicated tuple key — symptomatic of code submitted without a final read-through. Add the newline.

review.summary: The PR correctly identifies a real bug — an inner try/except around _process_messages converted websocket disconnects into a silently-swallowed exception, which the outer reconnect loop then spun on — and the structural fix of removing that try/except is sound. However, the fix is applied without stating the contract of _receive_messages (precondition, postcondition, termination), without auditing the outer reconnect loop where the actual infinite-loop invariant lives, and while leaving a second bare-Exception catch inside the async-for that is the same anti-pattern at a smaller scale. The expanded error-type handling contains a literal duplicate key (\"transcriber_error\" appears twice), which is direct evidence the set was assembled by copy-paste rather than reasoned from the documented specification; it should be a named module-level constant. Per-error-type log context has also been lost in the consolidation. Verdict: TESTED-NOT-PROVED with DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE residue — fix the duplicate, name the constant, state the contract, and confirm the outer loop's termination, then this is REASONED.
